section_summary: This section follows Japanese proposals for tighter control of the oil trade in Japan and Manchuria, including a state monopoly, licensing, refining plans, and sales quotas. American and British oil interests seek assurances that their investments and trade will remain viable, while U.S. officials consider possible diplomatic responses. The final despatch describes Soviet gasoline imports by Kojiro Matsukata and a proposed quota agreement that foreign companies fear will limit their growth.

subfiles.title: Answers concerning Japanese oil policy and the Important Industries Control Law
subfiles.about: Explains government support for domestic oil, control agreements, and the law's sales threshold.
subfiles.summary: The response describes ministerial oversight of gasoline industry agreements and circumstances in which controls could extend to smaller firms.

subfiles.title: Japan Makes Plans to Monopolize Oil
subfiles.about: Reports tentative Japanese plans for a state oil monopoly or a licensing system.
subfiles.summary: The article outlines alternative plans for government ownership or licensing, both with potential to displace foreign firms. Officials say the proposals are preliminary.

subfiles.title: Summary of despatch No. 384: Japan's Oil Problems
subfiles.about: Summarizes foreign concern over Japan's proposed oil controls.
subfiles.summary: Foreign companies fear monopoly or licensing plans could exclude them.

subfiles.title: The Oil Business in Manchuria
subfiles.about: Reports plans for a Japanese-backed Manchurian oil company, exploration, a refinery, and control of distribution.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes reported meetings involving Japanese military officers and oil firms, proposed drilling sites, and competing refinery locations. He says a licensing and price scheme might eventually squeeze foreign distributors out of Manchuria. The report stresses that much of the information remains rumor.

subfiles.title: Summary of despatch No. 399: The Oil Business in Manchuria
subfiles.about: Summarizes reports of a Manchurian oil company and possible restrictions on foreign distributors.
subfiles.summary: A proposed company would explore, refine, and possibly control oil distribution.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch No. 411
subfiles.about: Points to Grew's report on Japan's oil problems and the Economic Conference.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch No. 411.

subfiles.title: Japan's Oil Problems: Further Developments
subfiles.about: Forwards a proposal for oil industry talks in London during the Economic Conference.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports that Socony-Vacuum and Rising Sun want Japanese oil company representatives to meet American, British, and Dutch interests in London to protect foreign investments and trade.

subfiles.title: Socony-Vacuum cable proposing London oil talks
subfiles.about: Proposes international company talks before Japan adopts a restrictive oil policy.
subfiles.summary: The cable suggests a London meeting with Japanese companies and possible government support. It warns that monopoly, licensing, or a central company could harm foreign interests in Japan and Manchuria.

subfiles.title: Letter on Socony-Vacuum representation in London
subfiles.about: Offers to send a company representative to London for oil discussions.
subfiles.summary: Coe asks that the American delegation receive relevant information and says J. C. Goold could travel to London with about a month's notice.

subfiles.title: Japanese Government Oil Policy
subfiles.about: Transmits diplomatic correspondence about Japan's future policy toward foreign oil companies.
subfiles.summary: Goold lists three enclosed letters concerning British and American inquiries.

subfiles.title: Lindley letter about British oil interests
subfiles.about: Describes Lindley's appeal to Count Uchida for a policy welcoming British oil investment.
subfiles.summary: Lindley tells Uchida that British firms might invest more if reassured they would not be squeezed out. Uchida promises to convey the message.

subfiles.title: Goold thanks Grew
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Grew's discussion with Arita and thanks the embassy for assistance.
subfiles.summary: Goold thanks Grew and forwards his account to New York.

subfiles.title: Grew's discussion with Arita
subfiles.about: Reports an appeal concerning a gasoline tank and assurances for foreign oil investment.
subfiles.summary: Grew raises Socony-Vacuum's Uozaki tank and asks Arita to clarify future policy toward foreign companies.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Coe letter on London representation
subfiles.about: Repeats Coe's request for consultation with the American delegation in London.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the June 2 letter on Goold's possible London trip.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Japanese Government Oil Policy letter
subfiles.about: Lists correspondence enclosed for the New York office.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Goold's May 11 transmittal.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Lindley letter
subfiles.about: Repeats Lindley's account of his conversation with Count Uchida.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Lindley's April 13 letter seeking protection for British oil investment.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Grew's discussion with Arita
subfiles.about: Recounts Grew's discussion of Socony-Vacuum's tank and foreign oil policy with Arita.
subfiles.summary: Grew presses for permission to use the Uozaki tank or an equivalent arrangement and asks whether foreign oil companies can continue to invest and compete.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Goold's thanks to Grew
subfiles.about: Thanks Grew for his intervention with Arita.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Goold's May 11 acknowledgement.

subfiles.title: Third copy of Coe letter on London representation
subfiles.about: Repeats Socony-Vacuum's proposal to send Goold to London.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Coe's June 2 letter.

subfiles.title: Third copy of Japanese Government Oil Policy letter
subfiles.about: Again lists enclosed correspondence on Japanese oil policy.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Goold's May 11 transmittal.

subfiles.title: Third copy of Lindley letter
subfiles.about: Repeats Lindley's appeal to Count Uchida on behalf of British oil interests.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of Lindley's April 13 letter.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck replies to Coe about London discussions
subfiles.about: Advises oil interests to confer in London before taking unresolved issues to conference delegations.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck says the American delegation has the relevant reports. He suggests that company representatives first meet one another in London, then approach their delegations if they cannot settle the issues.

subfiles.title: Coe correspondence about a London visitor
subfiles.about: Concerns a Standard Oil representative's planned contact with the American delegation.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR is largely illegible; later correspondence identifies this as Coe's June 8 letter.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck forwards oil correspondence to Feis
subfiles.about: Sends Socony-Vacuum correspondence to the American delegation in London.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck forwards company letters and departmental replies about a proposed London representative.

subfiles.title: Reply to Coe about Henry Dundas
subfiles.about: Confirms that Feis has been informed of Dundas's intended visit.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck says Feis will be glad to discuss Japanese oil issues with Dundas.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding Socony-Vacuum correspondence
subfiles.about: Sends Grew copies of correspondence with Coe about the Japanese oil industry.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Coe's letters and departmental replies for the embassy's information.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to despatch No. 419
subfiles.about: Points to Grew's report on two Japanese oil control proposals.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to despatch No. 419.

subfiles.title: Extract on Japan's oil problems
subfiles.about: Summarizes proposed monopoly and licensing plans.
subfiles.summary: Extract notes that either plan could exclude foreign oil importers or refiners.

subfiles.title: Conference with Kersey F. Coe
subfiles.about: Records Coe's discussion with Hornbeck about protecting foreign oil interests in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Coe supplies memoranda and cables and advocates London talks among American, British, Dutch, and Japanese firms. Hornbeck arranges for the material to reach the American delegation and discusses the limited apparent legal basis for action.

subfiles.title: Possible claim arising from Japanese oil nationalization
subfiles.doc_type: Office of the Economic Adviser memorandum
subfiles.about: Considers whether Socony-Vacuum might have a claim if Japan violates prior permissions.
subfiles.summary: The writer advises awaiting developments, while identifying the company's original concession or construction permissions as potentially important evidence if nationalization harms its rights.

subfiles.title: Coe on a proposed Manchurian refinery application
subfiles.about: Seeks informal advice on British plans to approach Manchukuo and apply to build a refinery.
subfiles.summary: Coe reports Asiatic Petroleum's proposal to seek a refinery permit at Hulutao or Newchwang. He worries that approaching the unrecognized Manchukuo government could complicate Open Door diplomacy and asks for an unofficial opinion. He also describes contacts with Japanese Consul General Horinouchi.

subfiles.title: Coe on proposed Manchurian oil company and market shares
subfiles.about: Reports a proposed Manchurian refinery and restrictions on existing oil distributors.
subfiles.summary: Coe relays reports of a new Japanese-Manchurian company and a plan reserving half the market for its products. He gives Socony-Vacuum's existing gasoline and kerosene shares and fears significant losses. Conversations with Horinouchi and journalist James L. Young yield differing views of Japan's commitment to the Open Door.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Coe's July 19 letter
subfiles.about: Repeats concerns about Manchurian oil market allocation and Japanese policy.
subfiles.summary: Poorly legible duplicate of Coe's July 19 letter.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding Coe's July 19 letter
subfiles.about: Sends information on the proposed Manchurian oil company to the embassy.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Coe's letter and the Department's reply, with copies available for Mukden.

subfiles.title: Office review of Socony-Vacuum letters
subfiles.about: Reviews proposed replies to Socony-Vacuum's letters about Manchurian oil policy.
subfiles.summary: A draft reply would convey further reports from Mukden and Tokyo. After checking what the London delegation had discussed, the writer recommends delaying an informal opinion on approaching Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Internal opinion on forcing the Manchurian oil issue
subfiles.about: Advises against giving Socony-Vacuum a written informal opinion.
subfiles.summary: The writer considers an immediate Asiatic Petroleum challenge unwise and recommends waiting for further information after Secretary Hull's return.

subfiles.title: Coe updates the proposed Manchurian oil company
subfiles.about: Corrects the proposed company's capital figures and reports a Dairen refinery and sales plan.
subfiles.summary: Coe says Manchukuo's proposed stake is one million yen within a five-million-yen company. His Yokohama office reports military and railway disagreement over control, a refinery planned for Dairen, and a possible scheme assigning half the market to its products.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck acknowledges Coe's letters
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of Coe's July correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck promises official replies to the July 27 and 31 letters.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Coe's July 31 update
subfiles.about: Repeats the reported capital structure and refinery plan.
subfiles.summary: Poorly legible duplicate of Coe's July 31 letter.

subfiles.title: The Oil Business in Manchuria
subfiles.about: Reports more definite plans for a Dairen refinery and controlled sales in Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports a selected refinery site, five-million-yen capitalization, and a tentative plan guaranteeing the refinery half the Manchurian market. He describes unresolved questions about other companies' sales and continuing rivalry between the Japanese military and South Manchuria Railway.

subfiles.title: Review of despatch No. 507 on Soviet gasoline
subfiles.about: Comments on the market effect of Matsukata's Soviet gasoline imports.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum notes lower-priced Russian gasoline, possible Soviet financing, and concern that a revised quota agreement could disadvantage foreign companies.

subfiles.title: Summary of despatch No. 507: Japan's Oil Problems
subfiles.about: Summarizes Matsukata's imports and a new gasoline quota agreement.
subfiles.summary: Lower-priced Soviet gasoline alarms established firms; foreign companies fear restrictive quotas.

subfiles.title: Japan's Oil Problems
subfiles.about: Describes Soviet gasoline shipments, Matsukata's marketing, and a proposed Japanese gasoline quota agreement.
subfiles.summary: Neville reports that Matsukata has received a Soviet gasoline shipment, built storage at Tsurumi, found financing, and offered gasoline well below established retail prices. His success unsettles the six established firms and prompts discussion of extending industry controls. A proposed quota formula preserves current sales but gives the two foreign firms a smaller share of future growth; they see it as an initial step toward exclusion.
